# Internal short E owners force a paired consumer and admit simultaneous compensation

22 October 2026. Retain all H3 original endpoint/support/matching records,
the recurrence, and the explicit complete full-even-U/rotor model from
[the internal E barrier](SECONDARY_TEN_INTERNAL_E_BARRIER.md). In particular,
actual owners of all t_j=(a_j-4,s_j) and y_j=(a_j-1,C_j), C_j=s_j+w_j+13,
are distinct north-terminal full U originals. The internal y owner R_j
is left with incident depth d>=10. No arbitrary-grid catalogue exhaustion
or complete-extension existence is asserted.

## Actual-owner coupling at incident depth ten

Fix any internal j and write a=a_j,s=s_j,w=w_j,C=s+w+13.
Suppose its actual E owner has incident depth ten:

    R=U(L,10,f), chart(r,c)->(a-11+r,C+1-c), f>=4 even.

Then its actual t owner T necessarily has the form

    T=U(M,4,g), chart(r,c)->(a-8+r,s+1-c),
    M,g even, M>=6,g>=4, and L>=w+M+14.                 (1)

This classifies T's orientation and incident leg, and bounds its breadth;
it does not classify g or assert sufficiency. In particular L>=w+20.
The former tight R breadth w+14 is impossible at incident ten for EVERY
far depth, not merely the sampled negative-marginal example.

Proof. Put F=C+1-L, the R far column. R occupies all far-column rows
a-11,...,a-11+f, including a-8. P_j's bar row a-8 occupies every column
s+1,...,C-1. Since L>=6, F<=C-5, so endpoint disjointness forces F<=s,
equivalently L>=w+14. Every R bar point at row a-10 and columns F,...,C
is an endpoint, including (a-10,s).

The actual t owner has an incident column at s ending at row a-4. If
its even incident depth were at least six, that column would include
(a-10,s), colliding with R. Hence its depth is four. A right depth-four
t owner has bar endpoint (a-8,s+1), colliding with P. It must be left,
in the displayed chart. Its bar row a-8 occupies columns G=s-M+1,...,s.
R contains (a-8,F); since F<=s, avoiding T requires F<G, hence F<=s-M.
Substitution yields L>=w+M+14. All comparisons concern complete original
endpoint sets, including bar rows zero and one. The old same-color
terminal argument ensures R and T are distinct actual originals.

## A further restriction on the first remaining internal deep B branch

If j+1<n and a right actual t_(j+1) owner has breadth w+w_(j+1)+26
and incident D=z_j+6, the earlier internal depth gap forces its far
depth to equal four. Call this owner B. Its far column C occupies
[a-16,a-12]. Any E owner with d>=12 would contain (a-12,C), so the
actual R has d=10 and (1) applies.

Put v=w_(j+1) and s'=s-v-12. B's near column s' contains row a-10
because its incident interval is [a-16,a+z_j-10], with z_j>=24.
R's lower bar occupies [F,C] at that row. Thus F>s'. Both columns
are even, so F>=s'+2, and

    w+M+14 <= L <= w+v+24, hence M<=v+10.              (2)

This is a necessary finite WIDTH window inside an unbounded geometric
family; no full extension or sufficiency of (2) is asserted. The branch
is not eliminated merely because the previous D=z+4 branch was.

## Exact compensation when both far legs are four

Assume in addition f=g=4 for these actual R and T. Write

    L=w+M+14+q, q>=0 even, F=s-M-q, G=s-M+1.

For EVERY allowed H3 chain and internal j, the two displayed full
originals are endpoint-disjoint from ALL H3 and from each other. Their
selected-union increment relative to H3 is exactly

    DeltaPhi({R,T}|H3)=M-2*[q=0] >=4.                  (3)

Here Phi=N+S+2F_full-E_foreign, with immutable original source charges,
mixed full physical tiles and owner-labelled directed intratile events
excluding targets in the source's ORIGINAL support set. No arbitrary
exterior-owner monotonicity is used.

First verify geometric separation from ALL originals. R occupies rows
a-11,...,a-1, and T rows a-8,...,a-4. R's far column F<=s-6 lies
strictly left of every endpoint of block j and its west rotor/small U,
whose minimum column is s-4. T's far column G<=s-5 is also outside
their endpoints. At the limiting G=s-5, adjacency to old column s-4
crosses a physical tile-column boundary, so there is no intratile event.
R's far tip ends at a-7, before the current west rotor's first row a-5.
R and T bars lie above the original body, apart from T's near contact
with P; R's near column stops at y, immediately above old E at (a,C).

At all columns <=C, every earlier-block endpoint is at row at most a-16:
the nearest predecessor's small U ends at a-z_(j-1)+8<=a-16; its other
left-side body endpoints are higher. The predecessor's long V column
is C+1, across the physical tile boundary from odd C; the remaining
earlier long columns are farther right. Every later-block body starts
at least a_(j+1)-8>=a+10, and later long columns start still lower.
Thus no earlier/later original adds a same-tile receipt to R or T.
This accounts for the whole retained chain, not just P_j.

Each original's immutable charge is used ONCE. R has charge -1; T has
charge 1-M, giving added negative mass M and no positive-owner count.

R's near contact contributes exactly FOUR new full tile minima

    (a-7,C-1), (a-5,C-1), (a-3,C-1), (a-1,C-1),

and EIGHT directed events, both directions between (r,C-1) and (r,C)
for r=a-7,a-5,a-3,a-1. At the bottom, old E supplies the fourth cell
of the P/R/E tile; that tile is counted once. Both vertical R/E directions
are excluded by the two immutable original axial supports. These are the
left-phase receipts; the right-root E receipt has different event rows.

T's near contact contributes exactly TWO new full tile minima

    (a-7,s), (a-5,s),

and FOUR directed events, both directions between (r,s) and (r,s+1)
for r=a-7,a-5. These two tile columns and R's near column are distinct.

If q>=2, R's far column is at least three columns left of T's far
column G, with no endpoint-tile intersection; there is no R/T receipt.
If q=0, F is even and G=F+1. Their far-column overlap is exactly
the two rows a-8,a-7. At row a-8 both directions target original
supports and are excluded. At row a-7 both directions are counted,
giving exactly TWO new events. The tile at rows a-9,a-8 is missing
T's upper-right cell; the tile at a-7,a-6 is missing R's lower-left
cell. Neither is full. All other endpoints of R and T have disjoint
physical tiles. Hence

    DeltaS=M, DeltaN=0, DeltaF_full=6,
    DeltaE_foreign=12+2*[q=0],

which proves (3). Each tile/event is specified as a physical set element
with its original owner label, so the ledger does not depend on insertion
order or credit an old wall owner's mass again.

In the tight case q=0 there is a NEW forced support

    x=(a-6,F).

It is R's original far axial support, absent from H3,R,T endpoint sets.
Its north neighbor (a-7,F) belongs to R and east neighbor (a-6,F+1)
to T. A complete extension must therefore consume x with another actual
owner. This is an additional obligation; (3) does not assert local support
closure or construct a complete extension.

## Simultaneous compensation without repeated reserve

Fix a single complete extension and any subset J of INTERNAL blocks
whose actual R,T satisfy d_R=10,f_R=4,d_T=4,f_T=4. At each such block
the above necessity proves (1). The physical tile ROW footprint of its
new endpoints is

    [(a_j-11)/2,(a_j-1)/2].

For successive chain blocks a_(j+1)-a_j=z_j-6>=18. Thus the next row
footprint starts at least FOUR tile rows after the current footprint's
last row: (a_(j+1)-11)/2-(a_j-1)/2>=4. The same holds for any ordered
subset. These footprints are disjoint regardless of the bars' widths.
There is no new-new full tile or intratile event across pairs. Source
owners are distinct, old full tiles/events persist, and all new receipts
are the exact disjoint union of the per-pair sets above. Therefore

    Phi(H3 union all selected R_j,T_j)-Phi(H3)
      =sum_(j in J) (M_j-2*[q_j=0]) >=4*|J|.           (4)

This adds only NEW joint increments relative to the SINGLE H3 inventory.
It never adds old-prefix reserves. In particular the same original mass,
physical full tile or directed event is not credited twice. Other actual
owners and longer far legs still require their own analysis; no global
5/6 improvement or rectangular-grid triple equality follows yet.

## Verification scope

The companion verifier checks full-original actual-role decisions,
the narrow-depth collision and width coupling, exact physical receipt
SETS, tight forced supports, nonuniform translated chains and simultaneous
pair groups. Scoped Lean handles the coordinate collisions, necessary
width/depth bounds, receipt arithmetic and disjoint row footprints.
The actual-owner catalogue adapter and geometric receipt exhaustion remain
written proofs. Finite enumeration supplements these proofs.

# A predecessor barrier at every internal E support

22 October 2026. This note retains ALL H3 originals and the explicit
complete full-U/rotor model of
[the mandatory E-footprint theorem](SECONDARY_TEN_MANDATORY_E_FOOTPRINT.md).
Every actual original is a lattice-isometric full even U(L,d,f), L>=6,
d,f>=4, or a standard rotor. Original endpoints, supports and matching
are immutable; endpoints of different originals are disjoint; every
unconsumed original support has occupied degree one. No exhaustion of
arbitrary grid components by this catalogue is asserted.

## Statement

Let a_j be odd, s_j even, and all w_j>=12,z_j>=24 even, with

    a_j=a_(j-1)+z_(j-1)-6,
    s_j=s_(j-1)-w_j-12,
    C_j=s_j+w_j+13=s_(j-1)+1.

At EVERY internal index j>=1 in a complete extension, the actual owner
R_j of the old E support y_j=(a_j-1,C_j) is LEFT north-terminal:

    U(L,d,f), chart(r,c)->(a_j-1-d+r,C_j+1-c),
    10<=d<=z_(j-1)-10, with L,d,f even, L>=6,f>=4.       (1)

These are necessary conditions, not a full breadth/far-leg classification
or an existence assertion. In particular every such owner has original
charge -1 and contains ELEVEN consecutive endpoints

    {(r,C_j): a_j-11<=r<=a_j-1}.                         (2)

Only the first E owner can have positive charge. If n_L,n_R count all
E-owner phases, n_R<=1 and n_L>=n-1. The previously proved exact
immutable inventory remains Delta(N+S)=sum(L_j^(t)-1)+n>=6n; this
refinement allocates its E part as DeltaS_E=n_L, DeltaN_E=n_R.
It is not a net Phi bound.

For an internal j with j+1<n, a right actual t_(j+1) owner with breadth
w_j+w_(j+1)+26, incident depth D and far depth g necessarily satisfies

    D<=z_j-12   OR   D-g>=z_j+2.                         (3)

In particular D=z_j+4 is impossible for EVERY even g>=4. The first
possible deep incident depth is at least z_j+6, and at that depth g=4.
Neither surviving phase is asserted sufficient or completely extendible.

## Proof of the predecessor barrier

The mandatory-footprint theorem applies without alteration: y_j is
absent from H3, its west/south/east neighbors belong to retained different
originals, and completeness requires a fresh north-terminal consumer.
Both rotor roles collide with old endpoints. A U consumer is in one of
the two charts

    (r,c)->(a_j-1-d+r,C_j+1-c)  left,
    (r,c)->(a_j-1-d+r,C_j-1+c)  right.

Its incident column occupies EVERY row from a_j-1-d to a_j-1,
including bar rows zero and one. Left depths 4,6,8 collide with P_j.
A right owner has d>=z_(j-1)+2, because its lower bar endpoint at
(a_j-d,C_j+1) collides with V_(j-1) for every even d<=z_(j-1).

There is an additional retained original above this INTERNAL root:

    X_(j-1)=U(6,4,4),
    chart(r,c)->(a_(j-1)+2-r,s_(j-1)+2-c).

Its near column is s_(j-1)+1=C_j and includes all FIVE endpoints
at rows a_(j-1)-2,...,a_(j-1)+2, equivalently

    a_j-z_(j-1)+4,...,a_j-z_(j-1)+8.                     (4)

Since z_(j-1)>=24, the top row a_j-z_(j-1)+8 is above y_j.
The incident interval, which ends at y_j, can avoid (4) only by starting
strictly below that top row:

    a_j-1-d > a_j-z_(j-1)+8.

Thus d<z_(j-1)-9. Both depths are even, giving d<=z_(j-1)-10.
This applies to BOTH U orientations. It contradicts the necessary right
depth d>=z_(j-1)+2. The owner is left, and its previous lower bound
d>=10 proves (1). Its incident column then contains (2). The full-original
charge calculation in the cited theorem gives charge -1 independently
of breadth/far depth. Distinctness of the E owners and their distinction
from all t owners follow from that theorem's same-color terminal argument.
Consequently all n-1 internal E owners contribute to S, and only the
root owner can contribute to N. This proves the inventory assertions.

## Refined internal depth gap

Put a=a_j,C=C_j,z=z_j. The proposed right t_(j+1) owner B has far
column C and occupies its entire interval

    [a+z-10-D, a+z-10-D+g].                              (5)

It is distinct from R_j. Indeed, if B contained y_j on this column,
the next row a would also belong to its interval: y_j has even row
and the interval's last row is odd. That next point is a retained E_j
endpoint, contradicting endpoint disjointness. Therefore (5) must avoid
the eleven R_j endpoints AND the old endpoint (a,C), hence every row
in [a-11,a]. Both endpoints of (5) have the same odd parity as a.
Its last row must be at most a-12, or its first row at least a+2.
These alternatives are exactly D-g>=z+2 or D<=z-12, proving (3).
In the deep phase g>=4 gives D>=z+6; equality gives g=4.

For the earlier first-deep choice D=z+4, the far-column interval starts
at a-14 and, for every g>=4, contains (a-10,C). This point belongs
to R_j by (2). Thus it cannot occur at any internal root. In the
smallest case g=4, B ends at a-10, so it does not contain y_j and
the collision involves two distinct originals directly.

## What fails, and what remains valid

The first-root staircase and width-five stack theorems remain valid in
their stated scope. This result obstructs the proposed way to APPLY
the first-root package independently at all internal blocks. It does
not refute the target global inequality or the conditional additivity
of NEW stack increments on disjoint physical tile footprints.

The obstruction is stronger than an old-endpoint collision. For example,
take H3 at a_0=31,s_0=0,h=6, widths (12,12,12), depths (24,24,24).
Then j=1 has a=49,s=-24,C=1. The first-deep right t_2 candidate is

    B=U(50,28,4), chart(r,c)->(35+r,-49+c).

Its endpoints are disjoint from ALL H3 original endpoints. Nevertheless
it contains (39,1), while any actual R_1 must contain every (r,1)
for 38<=r<=48. Hence H3+B has NO complete feasible extension in
the stated model. This is a precise obstruction to that partial family's
complete extendibility, not a complete-family counterexample to Phi.

## Validation scope and next step

The companion verifier checks complete original endpoint/support/matching
records at varied internal indices, nonuniform dimensions and translations;
the predecessor's five points; both-orientation incident bounds; charge
phases; eleven-point inclusion; refined B decisions; and old-disjoint
but nonextendible first-deep candidates. The scoped Lean source proves
the coordinate barrier, orientation exclusion, interval gap and depth
consequences. Actual-owner normalization and the general charge inventory
use the written earlier theorem, not a finite census.

Exact controls pass 84 predecessor guards, 37,800 full-original U roles,
16,632 eleven-point inclusions and 13,536 refined depth-gap decisions.
There are 6,492 sampled old-disjoint left owners; 1,008 old-disjoint B
candidates fail the mandatory footprint, including 60 first-deep examples.
The displayed uniform example is checked separately. Standalone local
Lean passes 22 declarations, including 16 theorems, with individual axiom
reports, no warnings and no sorry/native axioms. The independent review
is running in the existing cavity/stack conversation; no verdict is
claimed. See the [validation record](../output/secondary-ten-internal-e-barrier-validation.json).

Next: classify the surviving internal LEFT E owners and their exact
joint receipts, including renewed support obligations. Any bulk allocation
must use actual internal configurations. No global 5/6 improvement,
complete-family allocation or rectangular-grid triple equality is claimed.
The submitted 11 October manuscript is unchanged.


FILE docs/SECONDARY_TEN_MANDATORY_E_FOOTPRINT.md
# An unavoidable E-owner footprint excludes both recent right-band families

21 October2026. Retain the full H3 originals, dimensions and recurrence of
[the right-band note](SECONDARY_TEN_RIGHT_BAND_FORCED_PREDECESSOR.md).
This note strengthens its far-phase obstruction. It also supersedes the
interpretation of the raised-band selected-union receipts as potentially
nonempty complete-family branches. Those exact receipts remain true for
partial inventories; the specified actual-owner hypotheses are impossible.

## Statement

Standing model hypothesis: EVERY actual original in the extension is a
lattice-isometric image of a FULL permitted U(L,d,f), with L,d,f all
even, L>=6,d,f>=4, or of the standard rotor. Every original retains its
complete endpoint, matching and original-support sets. The endpoint sets
are pairwise disjoint and every unconsumed original support has occupied
degree1. This is explicitly a complete feasible U/rotor-family theorem.
It does not assert that an arbitrary grid configuration has such a global
catalogue; an application beyond this model needs its own exhaustion proof.

For every old block j, write a=a_j,s=s_j,u=w_j and C=s+u+13. In ANY
complete feasible extension retaining H3, the original E_j support

    y_j=(a-1,C)

has a fresh actual owner R_j. That owner is a north-terminal U, with all
breadth/leg dimensions even, and its incident depth is at least8. Hence
the NINE consecutive sites

    K_j={(r,C): a-9<=r<=a-1}

all belong to R_j's original endpoint set. A left R_j has incident depth
at least10. A right R_j has depth at least8 at the first block; at a
noninitial block it has depth at least z_(j-1)+2. These are NECESSARY
conditions, not a complete classification or an existence assertion.

Consequently neither B=U(u+v+26,z,g) nor
B=U(u+v+26,z+2,g), in the charts of the unraised/raised notes, can be an
actual owner in a complete extension, for ANY geometrically allowed far
depth g. The unraised g4 case and the raised g4 case are excluded too.
The conditional gains>=22 and>=44 remain correct selected-union
identities, but their complete-family hypotheses have no instances.

More generally, fix the breadth u+v+26 of a right actual t_(j+1) owner,
and allow arbitrary even incident depth D>=4 and far depth g>=4. A
necessary complete-family condition is the dichotomy

    D<=z-12   OR   D-g>=z.                       (1)

Thus the first possible deep phase has D>=z+4; D=z+4 forces g4. No
sufficiency or complete extension in that phase is asserted.

## Why E's actual owner must be deep

The point y is absent from every old endpoint set and is E_j's original
axial support: E=U(6,4,4), chart(a+4-r,s+u+7+c), sends(5,6) to y.
It has three retained endpoint neighbors:

    west  (a-1,C-1) in P_j^0,
    south (a,C)     in E_j,
    east  (a-1,C+1) in the root if j=0,
                        or V_(j-1) if j>0.

For the first block the root occupies column C+1 continuously from
row a-6 through a, including its row0 bar endpoint. For j>0 the old V
far column is C+1 and is occupied from a-z_(j-1) through a. These
statements follow directly from the original charts and recurrence.
P's near column C-1 is occupied from a-8 through a+2.

Completeness forces y to be consumed: if it remained an unconsumed
original support its occupied degree would exceed1. Its owner is fresh,
and its matching neighbor can only be north. All three other neighbors
are already endpoints of retained different originals. In fact y has
exactly one own endpoint neighbor, since the matching supplies north.

The full-original U/rotor catalogue now applies at this terminal. Every
nonterminal U endpoint has at least two own endpoint neighbors. Leg
exchange gives the following two U charts, with L,d,f all even,
L>=6,d,f>=4:

    (r,c)->(a-1-d+r,C+1-c)   left,
    (r,c)->(a-1-d+r,C-1+c)   right.              (2)

The two north-terminal rotor endpoint sets, translated so y=(0,0), are

    {(-3,-1),(-2,-1),(-2,0),(-2,1),
     (-1,-2),(-1,-1),(-1,0),(0,0)},
    {(-3,1),(-2,-1),(-2,0),(-2,1),
     (-1,0),(-1,1),(-1,2),(0,0)}.

The first contains the retained west endpoint at(a-2,C-1); the second
contains the retained east endpoint at(a-2,C+1). Thus both are excluded.
This lists the full ORIGINAL rotor roles, not a cropped tip.

For a left U of incident depth d in{4,6,8}, its lower bar endpoint
(a-d,C-1) belongs to P: these rows are a-4,a-6,a-8, all in P's near
column including its row0 bar. Therefore left d>=10.

For right d4or6, its lower bar endpoint(a-d,C+1) is retained in the
root/earlier V. At the first block the root's row0 endpoint at a-6
is essential to excluding d6. At j>0 the same collision holds for
EVERY even d<=z_(j-1): the earlier V occupies that entire column
from a-z_(j-1) through a. Hence right d>=8 at j0, and
right d>=z_(j-1)+2 at j>0. In either frame d>=8.

The incident column of a full U occupies EVERY canonical row0,...,d:
the bar contributes rows0,1 and the leg contributes rows2,...,d.
Under(2) it therefore contains every site of K_j. This proves the
mandatory footprint without a finite cutoff or a guessed free-space rule.

## Exclusion of the two recent compensation branches

For B=U(u+v+26,z+2k,g), k0or1, the far column is C and its bar starts
at row a-10-2k. For every g>=4 its endpoint interval in that column
contains(a-8,C): the intrinsic row is2+2k, at most4. This point belongs
to R_j by the mandatory footprint.

For all geometrically allowed g, B ends at most at a-2 and so does NOT
contain y=(a-1,C). Its actual owner is therefore distinct from R_j.
The two full originals would share endpoint(a-8,C), impossible. If g
exceeds its geometric range, B already collides with retained E at(a,C).
Together these exclude every far-depth choice for k0and1.

This is stronger than the earlier g6/g8 matching obstruction. It does
not contradict the exact physical-tile/event receipts or their written
audits. It shows that these two conditional compensation branches are
vacuous in complete families and should be removed from the residual
search rather than counted as actual global compensation cases.

## The arbitrary-incident-depth necessary condition

For general D the right t_(j+1) owner has far-column interval

    [a+z-10-D, a+z-10-D+g] at column C.

It cannot contain any site of K_j, owned by the distinct R_j, or the
retained E endpoint(a,C). Thus the interval avoids ALL rows a-9,...,a.
Both interval endpoints have the same odd parity as a. Avoidance is
equivalent to ending at most a-10 or starting at least a+2. These are
precisely D-g>=z or D<=z-12, proving(1).

R_j is distinct because a geometrically admissible B cannot contain y:
if it contained y then the next row a would also lie in its far column
(its terminal parity is odd, whereas y has even row), colliding with E.
This also covers a bar starting below E; no depth cutoff is assumed.
Only necessity is claimed: old endpoint collisions and contacts can
further restrict either surviving phase.

## Distinct actual owners across the chain

Every y_j and every earlier forced t_j=(a_j-4,s_j) has odd row-plus-column
parity. Each is absent from H3 and can only be a north-terminal U endpoint;
the earlier t_j rotor exclusions are unchanged. The two terminals of a
full even U have OPPOSITE lattice colors: canonical(d,1) is odd and
(f,L) is even. A U therefore cannot own two of these same-color sites.
The t_j columns s_j strictly decrease. The y_j columns C_j also strictly
decrease, since C_j-C_(j+1)=w_j+12; moreover every t column is even and
every y column odd. Thus the 2n sites are distinct. Completeness requires at least2n distinct
fresh originals. Their physical-tile phases differ: t owners have odd
terminal row/even column, while y owners have even row/odd column.
Same checkerboard color does NOT imply the same original charge.

For a y owner put p=(d+f)/2. Its matching-edge count is L+p-1 in either
frame. In the left frame the bar occupies L/2 endpoint tiles and the
legs p more. The inward odd-row lateral supports contribute p-2, and
both axial supports lie in terminal endpoint tiles, giving p original
supports inside endpoint tiles. Thus charge=(L+p-1)+p-2*(L/2+p)=-1.

In the right frame the bar spans L/2+1 physical tile columns. The legs
add p tiles. The even-row lateral supports contribute p inside supports,
both axial supports contribute2 and both bar-exterior supports contribute2.
Thus charge=(L+p-1)+(p+4)-2*(L/2+1+p)=+1. These are FULL original
support counts, unchanged by consumption. Neither charge is1-L.

Let n_L,n_R count the y owners in the two frames. Then n_L+n_R=n,
DeltaS=sum_j(L_j^(t)-1)+n_L and DeltaN=n_R. Consequently the exact
immutable owner inventory is

    Delta(N+S)=sum_j(L_j^(t)-1)+n>=6n.

Every y owner contributes exactly1 to N+S; it contributes negative mass1
in the left frame or positive-owner count1 in the right frame. The earlier
claim that all2n owners have negative mass>=5 was a physical-phase error
and is withdrawn. This owner inventory is not a net global Phi bound:
mutual/exterior full-tile and directed-event receipts still need control.

import itertools
import json

from check_cooperative_promotion import neighbors
from check_demand_hull_reserve_obstruction import independent_source
from check_incident_eight_north_transfer import charge, shift
from check_secondary_ten_batch_terminal_budget import key, residual, transform
from check_secondary_ten_distinct_pair_consumers import east_rotor, upper_source
from check_secondary_ten_north_contact_debit import inventory
from rotor_networks import rotor, transform_module


if not __debug__:
    raise RuntimeError('Run without -O: verification uses assertions.')


def chain(origin, column_shift, widths, depths, root_breadth=6):
    assert widths and len(widths) == len(depths)
    assert origin % 2 == 1 and column_shift % 2 == 0
    assert root_breadth >= 6 and root_breadth % 2 == 0
    bases = []
    sites = []
    repairs = []
    previous_origin = previous_shift = None
    for index, (width, depth) in enumerate(zip(widths, depths)):
        assert width >= 12 and depth >= 24 and width % 2 == depth % 2 == 0
        if index:
            origin = previous_origin+depths[index-1]-6
            column_shift = previous_shift-width-12
        base = residual(origin, width, 10, depth)+[east_rotor(origin, width, True)]
        base = [shift(record, (0, column_shift)) for record in base]
        base_endpoints = set.union(*(record[0] for record in base))
        long_stem = {(row, column_shift+2)
                     for row in range(origin-4, origin+depth-5)}
        assert long_stem <= base[7][0]
        body = base_endpoints-long_stem
        assert all(origin-6 <= row <= origin+10 for row, column in body)
        assert min(column for row, column in base_endpoints) == column_shift+2
        assert max(column for row, column in base_endpoints) == width+17+column_shift
        if index:
            selected = shift(upper_source(origin, width, widths[index-1]+10,
                                         depths[index-1], 8, True), (0, column_shift))
            assert key(selected) == key(bases[-1][7])
        bases.append(base)
        sites.append((origin, width+14+column_shift, column_shift))
        repairs.append(independent_source((width+12, 10, 4),
                                         (False, False, True),
                                         (origin-8, width+13+column_shift)))
        previous_origin, previous_shift = origin, column_shift
    root = shift(upper_source(sites[0][0], widths[0], root_breadth, 6, 4, True),
                 (0, sites[0][2]))
    return bases, root, repairs, sites


def phi_from(records, receipt):
    return receipt['raw_reserve']+sum(charge(record) > 0 for record in records)

"""Full-original classification and exact simultaneous internal short-pair receipts."""

import itertools
import json

from check_cooperative_promotion import neighbors
from check_incident_eight_north_transfer import charge
from check_secondary_ten_arbitrary_t_consumers import north_U, old_chain
from check_secondary_ten_internal_consumer_chains import phi_from
from check_secondary_ten_north_contact_debit import inventory


if not __debug__:
    raise RuntimeError('Run without -O: verification uses assertions.')


def receipts(anchor, lateral, width, breadth, gap, old_owner, receiver_owner, consumer_owner):
    column = lateral+width+13
    far_column = lateral-breadth-gap
    full = {((anchor-7+2*index)//2, (column-1)//2) for index in range(4)}
    full |= {((anchor-7+2*index)//2, lateral//2) for index in range(2)}
    events = {(owner, source, target) for row in range(anchor-7, anchor, 2)
              for owner, source, target in (
                  (receiver_owner, (row, column), (row, column-1)),
                  (old_owner, (row, column-1), (row, column)))}
    events |= {(owner, source, target) for row in range(anchor-7, anchor-4, 2)
               for owner, source, target in (
                   (consumer_owner, (row, lateral), (row, lateral+1)),
                   (old_owner, (row, lateral+1), (row, lateral)))}
    if gap == 0:
        events |= {(receiver_owner, (anchor-7, far_column), (anchor-7, far_column+1)),
                   (consumer_owner, (anchor-7, far_column+1), (anchor-7, far_column))}
    assert len(full) == 6 and len(events) == 12+2*int(gap == 0)
    return full, events


def check_group(origin, offset, widths, depths, root_breadth, choices):
    fixed, bases, repairs, sites = old_chain(origin, offset, widths, depths, root_breadth)
    before = inventory(fixed)
    combined = list(fixed)
    expected_full, expected_events = set(), set()
    row_footprints = set()
    gain = 0
    for index, breadth, gap in choices:
        assert index >= 1
        anchor, unused, lateral = sites[index]
        width = widths[index]
        column = lateral+width+13
        receiver = north_U(anchor+3, column, width+breadth+14+gap, 10, 4, True)
        consumer = north_U(anchor, lateral, breadth, 4, 4, True)
        receiver_owner, consumer_owner = len(combined), len(combined)+1
        old_owner = 9*len(widths)+1+index
        full, events = receipts(anchor, lateral, width, breadth, gap,
                               old_owner, receiver_owner, consumer_owner)
        footprint = set(range((anchor-11)//2, (anchor-1)//2+1))
        assert not footprint & row_footprints
        row_footprints |= footprint
        assert not full & expected_full and not events & expected_events
        expected_full |= full
        expected_events |= events
        assert charge(receiver) == -1 and charge(consumer) == 1-breadth
        combined += [receiver, consumer]
        gain += breadth-2*int(gap == 0)
        if gap == 0:
            far_column = lateral-breadth
            target = anchor-6, far_column
            endpoints = set.union(*(record[0] for record in combined))
            assert target in receiver[1] and target not in endpoints
            assert {(anchor-7, far_column), (anchor-6, far_column+1)} <= (
                set(neighbors(target)) & endpoints)
    after = inventory(combined)
    assert after['full']-before['full'] == expected_full
    assert after['events']-before['events'] == expected_events
    assert before['full'] <= after['full'] and before['events'] <= after['events']
    assert after['mass']-before['mass'] == sum(breadth for index, breadth, gap in choices)
    assert phi_from(combined, after)-phi_from(fixed, before) == gain >= 4*len(choices)
    return dict(blocks=len(widths), pairs=len(choices), gain=gain,
                new_full=len(expected_full), new_events=len(expected_events))


def classification_controls():
    decisions = old_disjoint = pair_disjoint = tight_collisions = deep_windows = 0
    for width, previous_depth, current_depth in itertools.product((12, 40), (24, 80), (24, 80)):
        widths, depths = [12, width, 20], [previous_depth, current_depth, 24]
        fixed, unused, unused, sites = old_chain(31, 0, widths, depths, 6)
        blocked = set.union(*(record[0] for record in fixed))
        anchor, unused, lateral = sites[1]
        column = lateral+width+13
        for receiver_breadth, far in itertools.product(
                (6, width+12, width+14, width+16, width+20, width+40), (4, 6, 20)):
            receiver = north_U(anchor+3, column, receiver_breadth, 10, far, True)
            if receiver[0] & blocked:
                continue
            assert receiver_breadth >= width+14
            old_disjoint += 1
            for breadth, incident, other, left in itertools.product(
                    (6, 8, 20), (4, 6, 8, 10, 40), (4, 6, 20), (False, True)):
                consumer = north_U(anchor, lateral, breadth, incident, other, left)
                if not consumer[0] & (blocked | receiver[0]):
                    assert left and incident == 4 and receiver_breadth >= width+breadth+14
                    pair_disjoint += 1
                if receiver_breadth == width+14:
                    mandatory = {(row, lateral) for row in range(anchor-8, anchor-3)}
                    assert receiver[0] & mandatory
                    tight_collisions += 1
                decisions += 1
        next_anchor, unused, next_lateral = sites[2]
        parent = north_U(next_anchor, next_lateral, width+widths[2]+26,
                         current_depth+6, 4, False)
        for receiver_breadth, incident, far in itertools.product(
                range(6, width+widths[2]+36, 2), (10, 12, 14, 24), (4, 6, 20)):
            receiver = north_U(anchor+3, column, receiver_breadth, incident, far, True)
            if not receiver[0] & (blocked | parent[0]):
                assert incident == 10 and receiver_breadth <= width+widths[2]+24
            deep_windows += 1
    return dict(actual_role_decisions=decisions, old_disjoint_receivers=old_disjoint,
        pair_disjoint_survivors=pair_disjoint, tight_breadth_mandatory_collisions=tight_collisions,
        next_deep_window_decisions=deep_windows)


def main():
    exact = 0
    for origin, offset, width, breadth, gap in itertools.product(
            (-33, 31), (-100, 200), (12, 50), (6, 8, 20, 100), (0, 2, 10, 100)):
        check_group(origin, offset, [12, width, 20], [24, 80, 26], 40, [(1, breadth, gap)])
        exact += 1
    batches = []
    for count in (3, 6, 12, 24):
        widths = [12+2*((3*index) % 13) for index in range(count)]
        depths = [24+2*((7*index) % 17) for index in range(count)]
        choices = [(index, 6+2*(index % 5), 0 if index % 2 else 4) for index in range(1, count)]
        batches.append(check_group(31, -100, widths, depths, 6, choices))
    print(json.dumps(dict(status='PASS', classification=classification_controls(),
